determinatio est actus transiens, et tem-

voluntas in tempore, accedente potentia Dei
executrice, se determinaret. Primo hinc di-
co, falsæ funt hæ propositiones. 1. Deus de-
crevit ut effectus contingentes fierent necessa-
rio. 2. Deus decrevit ut actus liberi non po-
ssent non esse. Veræ funt hæ. Deus decrevit
ut effectus contingentes ita fierent, ut pos-
sent non fieri, nempe oblata suppositione æ-
ternæ futuritionis, & decreti divini. 3. De-
us decrevit ut illi actus liberi essent præcise &
non alii quam libertas liberè elicit in tempore.
Hinc etiam hæ propositiones observentur. 1.

page.notes: The last line is hyphenated "an-" and the catchword "tece-" stands at the foot right; the catchword reading is uncertain. The header "Contins." is read from a small-capitals running head. Some words in the first lines are set in a worn type, so "se" and "posito" are doubtful readings, and the sentence "ut dicens" sections are not fully legible. Edge fragments on the right margin belong to the neighbouring page and were left out.
